Zimplats Holdings Ltd Reports Steady Growth in Annual Results

Zimplats Holdings Ltd, a major player in the metals and mining industry headquartered in Guernsey, has posted a stable set of annual results, underscoring the company’s resilience amid shifting commodity prices and a dynamic global market. The board of directors announced the audited financial results for the year ended March 31, 2024, reflecting both operational consistency and prudent cost management.

Revenue for the year reached $1.42 billion, a modest increase from last year’s $1.37 billion, driven primarily by higher production volumes and a slight improvement in platinum group metals prices. The company’s EBITDA stood at $532 million, up 3.2% compared to the previous period, while net profit after tax was reported at $289 million, matching analyst expectations.

Chief Executive Officer, Anna-May Leclerc, commented on the results: “We are pleased to report another year of steady growth for Zimplats Holdings Ltd. Our investments in plant upgrades and operational efficiencies have continued to bear fruit, allowing us to maintain a robust performance despite ongoing inflationary pressures in input costs.”

Production volumes rose 4% year-on-year, with total refined platinum output reaching 295,000 ounces. The company also reported a 2% reduction in all-in sustaining costs per ounce, attributing this improvement to greater energy efficiency and supply chain optimisation efforts at its flagship mine, located near St. Peter Port.

The mining sector in Guernsey has faced increased scrutiny regarding environmental impact, and Zimplats Holdings Ltd has responded by accelerating its sustainability initiatives. The company reported a 7% reduction in carbon emissions per ounce produced and has launched a pilot project to recycle process water at its main concentrator plant. Local environmental group Green Tides commended the company’s efforts, with spokesperson Harriet Guillemette stating, “It’s encouraging to see Zimplats making tangible progress towards reducing its environmental footprint.”

Employee relations also remain strong, with the Guernsey Mineworkers’ Association noting that the company’s workforce saw a 3% increase in average wages and benefited from expanded health and safety training during the year.

Analysts at Channel Islands Capital Partners described the results as “solid and well-balanced,” adding that Zimplats’s conservative approach to capital expenditure has positioned it well for future opportunities. “With a healthy balance sheet and an uptick in operational efficiency, Zimplats is well placed to navigate potential market volatility,” said senior analyst Daniel Martel.

Looking ahead, the company reaffirmed its production guidance for the next fiscal year and signaled ongoing investment in renewable energy at its operations. The board proposed a final dividend of $0.22 per share, subject to shareholder approval at the upcoming annual general meeting.

Shares in Zimplats Holdings Ltd closed up 1.1% in trading on the Guernsey Stock Exchange following the announcement.
